topStories.headline: Chinatown's Connie Chan Concedes Congressional Race to Scott Wiener
topStories.dek: The San Francisco supervisor, who built her campaign partly on her roots in Chinatown, acknowledged Wednesday she no longer has a path to Congress.
topStories.body:
Supervisor Connie Chan conceded the race to succeed former Rep. Nancy Pelosi on Wednesday afternoon, November 5, clearing the way for state Sen. Scott Wiener to become San Francisco's next member of Congress. With an estimated 57 percent of ballots counted, Wiener led Chan 55.5 percent to 44.5 percent — a margin that Chan said she did not see narrowing enough to overturn.

The race carried unusual weight for Chinatown. Chan, who was born in Hong Kong and moved to San Francisco's Chinatown as a teenager, had framed her candidacy around the possibility of electing the first Chinese American to represent San Francisco in Congress. She campaigned through Chinatown's streets, prayed at Kong Chow Temple on Stockton Street in the final days of the race, and drew deep support from Chinese American voters across the city.

On election night, Chan told supporters that her mother — who immigrated to Chinatown about three decades ago — could not have imagined her daughter coming this close to a seat in Congress. In her concession statement she vowed to keep organizing around affordability, immigrant rights, and workers' issues.

Wiener thanked Chan for a hard-fought campaign and said he is ready to take on housing, health care, and transit at the national level. His win ends a nearly four-decade stretch in which Pelosi held the seat and marks the first time the district has seen a competitive general election in that span.

topStories.headline: Portsmouth Square Fences Stay Up — and Chinatown Merchants Are Feeling It
topStories.dek: Five months into the $73 million renovation of Chinatown's beloved public square, nearby business owners say the construction toll is proving harder to absorb than expected.
topStories.body:
Portsmouth Square — long known as the living room of San Francisco's Chinatown — broke ground on a two-year, $73 million overhaul on June 9, 2026, the first major renovation of the 1.3-acre park in nearly 50 years. The park closed the following day, and construction fencing has lined its perimeter ever since.

The project, expected to run through roughly fall 2028, will deliver a new flexible outdoor event space, a larger community clubhouse, a consolidated playground with adult fitness equipment, improved ADA access, public art, and new landscaping. It is funded through city bond money and state and local grants, with costs rising from $66 million when the project was approved in 2022 to $73 million today.

But the construction has arrived alongside two other major infrastructure projects in the same few blocks: an upgrade to the Chinatown Public Health Center and a renovation of the Chinatown/Him Mark Lai Branch Library, both of which also carry estimated 30-month timelines. The simultaneous work has brought parking disruptions, noise, and street-access complications that merchants say are cutting into foot traffic during what should be a busy season. The San Francisco Chronicle reported in August that some business owners were already questioning whether they could survive the two-year stretch.

City officials have acknowledged the strain. San Francisco Public Works has said that if investigation shows construction caused property damage to businesses, the city will make affected owners whole. The Portsmouth Square garage at 733 Kearny Street remains open throughout the renovation and continues to provide the main parking access into the neighborhood.

topStories.headline: Jupiter Room on Polk Still Dark — but 'Late 2026' Window Is Narrowing
topStories.dek: Chef Peter Hemsley and mixologist Trevin Hutchins have yet to open their much-anticipated martini bar at 2065 Polk, with the former Lord Stanley space still unfinished heading into November.
topStories.body:
As of early November, Jupiter Room — the martini-focused bar and restaurant planned for the former Lord Stanley space at the corner of Broadway and Polk Street on Russian Hill — has not opened. The bar's own website continues to list a 'late 2026' launch, and the most recent on-the-ground reporting from October 1 found the windows at 2065 Polk still papered over.

The project is a partnership between Michelin-starred chef Peter Hemsley, whose seafood restaurant Aphotic closed in 2024, and bar director Trevin Hutchins. The concept centers on culinary-driven martinis and elevated comfort food including burgers and shrimp cocktail. Before construction began, the bar was named to Imbibe magazine's global 'Imbibe 75' list of people and places shaping beverage culture, raising neighborhood expectations considerably.

Jupiter Room had originally targeted summer 2026, a deadline it missed. The official website was updated to 'late 2026,' which leaves a shrinking runway. Interested readers can follow updates at instagram.com/jupiter.room or at jupiter-room.com.

moreNews.headline: Chinatown's Three-Project Construction Marathon: What's Being Built and When
moreNews.body: San Francisco announced in July 2026 that three major infrastructure upgrades are under simultaneous construction in Chinatown: the renovation of Portsmouth Square (groundbreaking June 9, 2026, expected completion fall 2028); an upgrade to the Chinatown Public Health Center; and a renovation of the Chinatown/Him Mark Lai Branch Library. The health center and library projects each carry estimated 30-month timelines from the July 2026 announcement. City officials described the trio as 'once-in-a-generation upgrades.' Multilingual construction updates and traffic information are being provided by SF Public Works at sfpublicworks.org.
